question: Was the parent model's early I-70 threshold crossing (model hour 16.4 = 2026-08-20T10:25Z) the SAME causal mechanism that closed I-70 at hour 28 (22:00Z)? Case A = genuinely predictive fluvial pathway; Case B = coincidental early local wetting.
verdict: CASE B — the early signal is NOT the fluvial pathway that closed the road.
confidence: high for the parent (60 m) signal; nest dynamics pending as confirmation of mechanism, not of direction

evidence.argument: A routed flood wave cannot reach a downstream point before its own upstream peak. The parent declared I-70 impassable 2.6 h BEFORE the upstream South Fork gauge at Kirkersville even peaked, and 26 h before the crest at the crossing itself. The signal therefore cannot be the wave that closed the road.
evidence.source: NOAA NWM v3 analysis_assim (USGS-nudged) + NWS/press anchors

evidence.argument: The single 60 m cell at the I-70/South Fork crossing carries a bed 2.07 m below the true carriageway, roughly midway to the channel invert. When that cell reports 0.30 m ('impassable'), its water surface is still 1.77 m BELOW the real pavement. The parent is reporting channel/floodplain water as road inundation.
evidence.source: USGS 3DEP 1 m LiDAR vs the 60 m resampled parent grid

bias_direction.headline: Smearing inflates apparent Case A at stream crossings, and suppresses detection where the coarse bed sits above the pavement.
bias_direction.net: 3 of 12 corridor probes generate false 'impassable' declarations; 4 of 12 would miss real road flooding. A 60 m screening grid is therefore NOT usable for road-level closure decisions in either direction.

consequence_for_the_earlier_claim: The previously reported '+695 min lead time' on the I-70 closure is RETRACTED as a like-for-like warning claim. The model was not 11.6 h early on the same event; it was signalling a different (pluvial/channel) mechanism at a location whose coarse-grid elevation is not the road surface.
what_the_model_genuinely_could_not_do: Reproduce the delayed fluvial crest at all: the extended 56 h parent decays at the drainage-proxy rate (0.005 m/hr) instead of rising to the hour-43 crest. Two structural causes: (a) the scalar storm-drain term bleeds routed river water; (b) no lake storage, dam/spillway operation, baseflow, or upstream-of-domain inflow is represented. The 28 h observed routing lag is outside the model's physics as configured.
pending: Corridor nests at 6-8 m will show whether the carriageway cells themselves wet at the flash peak — confirming mechanism. Direction of the finding does not depend on them.
